chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) regarding the man who claims and has no proof for him.
He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is made to swear an oath, so if he turns the oath upon the owner of the right, and he does not swear, then there is no right for him.'

key_terms.فَلَا حَقَّ لَهُ: So there is no right for him
key_terms.يَسْتَحْلِفُهُ: He makes him swear an oath

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a defendant refuses to swear and turns the oath to the claimant who has no proof?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of *al-yamin* (oath) in Shia jurisprudence, where the burden of proof shifts to the defendant who is asked to swear to the truth of his denial. If the defendant refuses the oath and instead demands the claimant swear, the claimant's failure to do so results in the loss of his right, highlighting the procedural weight of the oath in resolving evidentiary disputes. This mechanism underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the oath as a decisive legal tool when documentary or testimonial evidence is absent.
